claims.claim: in interior Maine, bald eagles favor chain pickerel among their freshwater prey
claims.note: The abstract names three favored freshwater foods together: brown bullhead, white sucker and chain pickerel. Singling out pickerel goes beyond the abstract unless the full text ranks it first.

claims.claim: in interior Maine, fish made up 79 % of bald eagle prey items, with brown bullhead, white sucker and chain pickerel the favored freshwater foods
claims.note: The abstract says 'Fish comprised 79% of the food items collected in interior Maine' and names the three species as favored foods in freshwater habitats; food remains collected at 78 breeding and wintering areas, 1976–80, nearly 1,400 prey individuals. The abstract warns that fish are often under-rated in food-debris collections, so the 79 % is likely a minimum.

claims.claim: interior Maine bald eagles took fish as 79 % of prey items, chiefly brown bullhead, white sucker and chain pickerel

notes: Full text blocked. The abstract agrees with every number the paper uses (79 % fish in interior Maine; bullhead, sucker and pickerel favored), but the paper should say 'food items in remains collected at nests and roosts' and note the authors' caveat that remains under-represent fish. §3.7.7's 'favor chain pickerel' should list all three species unless the full text ranks pickerel first. MDIFW's bald eagle species assessment (Todd 2004, https://www1.maine.gov/ifw/docs/species_planning/birds/baldeagle/speciesassessment.pdf, fetched as Todd_etal_1982.mdifw-assessment.pdf) is not a stand-in: it gives only 'typical prey in interior Maine' (pickerel, bullhead, suckers, white and yellow perch) citing Todd et al. 1982 together with Welch 1994.
